diagnosis: TED's 2008 monthly packages ship each notice once per language, all with a DTD the parser declines. The non-English members are duplicates of an English original we already hold and parsed, so they are not lost data and were never a coverage gap - they are marked skipped-by-policy rather than reclaimed, because reclaiming them would claim ~593k notices entered the corpus that never did. Measured: 592,856 markable, verified against the English original being present AND parsed for every one.

category: 2008 siblings whose original did not parse
diagnosis: 154 of the 2008 held siblings have an English original that is held but did NOT parse, so the duplicate argument does not apply to them: nothing readable was recovered. They stay OUTSTANDING and are tracked as their own finding rather than swept in with the duplicates. Held-but-unextracted, not lost - we have the bytes and failed to read them, which is a parse defect to fix, not data to mourn. The sibling guard rejects them by construction, so the marker cannot absorb them.

1,898 rows carrying the same DTD label come from a single fetch - TED monthly 2010-03 - and are NOT language siblings at all: their member paths end .xml with no language code, where every 2008 row carries a 2-letter language. The duplicate-sibling reasoning cannot be applied to them, and they are outside the 2008 scope the marker requires, so they stay OUTSTANDING and untouched. Found only by attributing the remainder: every earlier query was scoped to 2008, and that scoping hid them. Needs its own investigation - start by establishing what these files are, not by re-running the sibling test.
Annex-D negotiated-procedure awards publish their justification as a @REASON attribute no rule claimed, so the whole award was held; REASON is now a captured attribute.
The RP authority code was scalar, but international-financing records list each co-financier on a continuation line; RP is now per-line, so every institution is kept.

The 1995-98 text vintages carry the main object CPV as OC (paired with the English description ON), which no rule claimed, quarantining the whole notice; OC is now claimed as CPV codes and ON as its description.

The 2008 OPOCE export is real S-series notices behind a DTD (INTERNAL_OJS R2.0.5) that roxmltree refused wholesale; the DTD is now safely stripped. The era ships each notice ONCE PER LANGUAGE, so the ~593k that remain held are the ~22 non-English duplicate siblings of the ~27k English notices, which are themselves present and parsed — verified row by row, 5,000 of 5,000 sampled, on two snapshots 29h apart. These are duplicates already ingested, NOT missing data, and no reprocess can move them: dispatch skips a non-English sibling by the one-notice-per-language policy, so it yields no record to reclaim. Their outstanding count therefore overstates the remaining work; the rows are stale bookkeeping from before the DTD fix.

The INTERNAL_OJS R2.0.5 era (~28k opoce-only S-series notices, the whole 2008 coverage gap) had no mapping profile and was held as a tracked unmapped-era. It is now parsed by the internal-ojs profile: a new envelope reader for the BIB_INFO/BIB_DOC_S coded backbone plus an explicit _SUM alias shim that reuses the r209 walker for the 85%-shared form body. Reprocessing the bucket reclaims the era into notices.

eForms notices declaring an SDK version (1.0-1.11) whose fields.json we had not vendored were held whole as unknown-customization - by far the largest bucket. All versions are now vendored (1.8-1.11 directly; 1.0-1.7 also needed an xpath grammar extension for descendant-axis and boolean-or predicates plus a predicate-free BT-165 binding), and the reprocess mechanism reclaims each held notice from the archive in place. The recovery rebuild (ADR-0009) folds them into the tender layer.

German eForms-DE 1.0/1.1/1.2 notices were held as unknown-customization - the SDK-DE fork is not on OP-TED's GitHub. Vendored from an empirical field inventory (issue 75), plus grafts for the DOE JAXB serializer's structural quirks: parties the SDK references by id are inlined instead (nested UBO under efac:Organization, an inlined AppealTerms recipient), so six gap-fill aliases graft them back (issue 78). The reprocess mechanism reclaims them; the recovery rebuild (ADR-0009) folds them in.
